pr_title: cli: skip excluded node in debug zip
pr_body:
Previously, debug zip cli command generates node directory with format `nodeID.skipped` for excluded nodes. It was causing confusion in analysing debug zip artifacts. To address this, this patch skips CPU profiles and directory generation for excluded nodes.

Epic: CRDB-32134
Fixes: #128590
Release note: None

issue_context.title: Cockroach debug zip --nodes flag still creates node-level folders and CPU profiles for skipped nodes
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

Using the `--nodes` flag for the `debug zip` command leads to some misleading behavior. Node-level folders will be created for nodes not explicitly included with that flag, and the debug zip command will still get CPU profiles for each node in the cluster.

**To Reproduce**

For any cluster, run the `cockroach debug zip` command with the `--nodes` command. In my example, I have a 24.1.2 3-node cluster and I ran the following such that node 3 is skipped:

```
cockroach debug zip debug.zip --nodes=1,2 --insecure
```

The debug zip command will still reach out to each node in the cluster and get a `cpu.pprof` regardless of this `--nodes` flag. It will always then create a folder for each node, as well as a `<node_id>.skipped` file for each node not included in the `--nodes` flag:

```
debug/nodes % ls
1		2		3		3.skipped
```

This is misleading, and perhaps a bit problematic. We still spend time reaching out to those nodes for data and create a node-level folder for each node that is supposed to be excluded.

**Expected behavior**

I would expect there to be no node-level folder or CPU profile for nodes I don't care to get info from via the debug zip.

This is pretty minor, but confusing behavior.

**Additional data / screenshots**

n/a

If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

**Environment:**

I believe this applies to all versions, but only tested in 24.1.
